before: I used to be all personal trainer and teach persistence on this as the remedy. Keeping at it does help, since a little one who learned to expect being dropped won't trust you right away. But I don't think that explains the adult feeling fully. More importantly, I think it could even be like unintentional gaslighting to the little one to ask to connect with them when you don't believe they're even real. Like when my mom pretended to listen to me when I was young, but even less excusable (from the inner child's view) because she was not asking for my time when she did that. So, it's worth meditating first on why it feels fake.

## The Parent You Inherited

I'd look at the parent "script" you inherited: how you learned to treat yourself from how people treated you growing up, long before you started building your Nurturer, Protector and Guide. It can be warm, but it's often more like a critic, or a warden with rules. The rules can even sound reasonable, like "You can come back to the table when you're done with your embarrassing crying fit." If yours was like that, your little one learned bit by bit to hide that part of their authentic self which wasn't allowed, so they could keep belonging. They might still be doing it.
guide_passage: For some people, the adult voice can stay fake in ordinary consciousness and become real only in an altered state. The child may suddenly feel unmistakably present; love, grief, innocence, or protection that sounded like therapy language can become emotionally obvious. If that happens, don’t throw it away afterward just because your sober mind cannot reproduce the feeling. Also don’t turn the intensity into proof that every image or memory is literal. The next task is transfer: can any of what became real remain available in ordinary life?
next: The Parent You Inherited: Before you deliberately build the Nurturer, Protector, and Guide, you usually already have a learned way of treating yourself: the inner parent “script” you inherited from how you were treated.
